description: IPv6 conformance vectors for the special-range policy (backlog E1-001). docs/03-applications/04-orchestrator-spec.md requires public IPv4/IPv6 rejection and rejection of encoded or alternate address representations. No vector here is scope-eligible: the scope record has no IPv6 target field and none of its patterns accept an IPv6 literal, so an IPv6 destination can only arrive through DNS resolution or a redirect, which is exactly where the runtime must classify it.

vectors.rationale: IPv6 loopback. Safe to reach but not expressible in a scope, so it is never eligible.
Uncompressed form of ::1. Two spellings of one address must classify alike.
The unspecified address. Binding it exposes every interface.
Link-local unicast. The denylist rejects link-local endpoints independently of scope.
Zone identifier attached to a link-local address. The zone does not make it routable.
Unique local address, the IPv6 analogue of RFC 1918. Private, but the scope cannot name it.
The whole unique-local block.
Global unicast. Public IPv6 rejection is a required safety test.
Global unicast resolver. Reachable from the lab and out of bounds.
Reserved for documentation. Not assigned, so not a lab target either.
All-nodes link-local multicast. Multicast is denied outside an isolated wireless profile.
IPv4-mapped loopback. An implementation must map it back to IPv4 before classifying, never accept it as written.
IPv4-mapped public address. This is the alternate representation that defeats a check reading only the IPv4 text form.
IPv4-mapped private address. Even the safe one is ineligible: a scope names the IPv4 form or nothing.
NAT64 well-known prefix carrying a public IPv4 address. A second way to write a destination the policy denies.
An IPv6 literal in a URL must be bracketed. Unbracketed it is not a URL at all.
Bracketed IPv6 loopback URL. Well formed and still ineligible, because the scope URL pattern admits no bracketed host.
Public IPv4 address disguised as an IPv6 literal inside a URL.
Non-hexadecimal digit in a group.
Two compressions. The expansion is ambiguous, so the literal has no single meaning.
Prefix length above 128.
